reviews.title: An abysmal experience
reviews.text: What in the actual F? I’m glad that somehow Microsoft’s product managers have found a way around actually having to use their own products. I wish they would show me how to do so as well. Unfortunately that obviously means they don’t actually understand what their users go through. I have a 5 license MS365 subscription. I am trying to open a CSV file on my iPad. First MS demands I change my permissions, but in typical MS fashion, isn’t clear / doesn’t provide adequate detail to understand what I should do and why I should do it.  After going through that adventure in idiocy, I then went to open Excel. I signed in using facial recognition, it actually recognized me, then proceeded to act like I hadn’t signed in and I was a “Guest” all the while showing that I was logged into my account. Meanwhile, there was no message that, perhaps my subscription had expired. No, just hi I recognize you but you still can’t have access to use the tool the world demands you use yet somehow we aren’t called a monopoly. What a joke.

reviews.title: Annoying login and subscription management
reviews.text: I have an account and subscription, but this app doesn’t keep me logged in, so when I open spreadsheets, they are usually read-only and I’m prompted to log in with a subscription. That would be bad enough, if it didn’t try to actually get me to pay an in-app purchase when I logged in… but it does. I can’t just log in and see “you have a subscription already,” I log in and see nothing but payment options despite already having a paid subscription, and it automatically tries to initiate an in-app payment. It’s just a barrage of things popping up at me that I have to cancel, say no, dismiss, close… so frustrating! But wait, we’re not done. No. Even the login process itself is full of interruptions and nags! It automatically tries to get my device to save a passkey for login. It’s not as if there’s just an option to generate a passkey; no, it’s worse; a passkey is being forced upon me, and I have to cancel, which is really confusing due to the way they’ve designed it, and this is all ANOTHER five or six steps to get through. And after all that, I STILL don’t have a functioning app. I have to force-kill the app and reopen my files to finally be able to edit them with the subscription and account that should have been active 5-8 minutes ago when I first opened my files! The way Microsoft has designed this just feels SO hostile and inconsiderate to me.

reviews.title: Microsoft!
reviews.text:
No, I don’t want to leave a review. No, I don’t want to dismiss this message every time I open the Excel app, or Outlook, or Teams, or anything else!! I just want to view a file. This prompt is preventing me from doing my job and is wasting my time. 


The app has a purpose. Why are you adding things that prevent the purpose??? Forcing me to respond to a “would you like to leave a review” prompt is no better than “accept or reject cookies” on most browsers. You are wasting people’s time. Nobody wants to leave a review. If you keep doing this, I will keep giving one star reviews to further deflate the purpose you are trying to achieve. 

You may say: “well, isn’t leaving this review wasting your time even more? It only takes a few seconds to dismiss the prompt.” To that I say, I will never go out of my way to leave a review - good or bad. If you prompt me, you get one star. Beg more, get less in return. 

I think this would be a perfect scenario: 1) download app 2) use app when you need it 3) app opens what you expect it to. That third step is key, isn’t it?? Isn’t that why we have the app in the first place? If you don’t open what I expect, how could YOU expect 5/5 stars and repeat customers? If this cost me $$$ I would use a different service.

BTW, even though you created Outlook and Excel, how come I can never view Excel files in Outlook on mobile? It’s extremely buggy and requires me to open the files in a separate app. Total time waster. Especially when you add review pr

reviews.title: Only saves your changes about 50% of the time
reviews.text: Where to start. 1.) when opening a file, it usually opens the last version you used on the ipad, NOT the updated one from the cloud, and thanks to autosave being on by default, by the time you notice you’re seeing an old copy, it auto saves over the current version, thereby actively destroying your work. Workaround? Open the file, close immediately, open again. It’s a hassle, like everything in this app, but it works. 2.) After you work for a while, for various long-winded reasons, the app seems to have a 50% chance of just deciding to lock up, give you a greyed out screen, and sometimes a message saying “closing ____.xlxs” with a little spinning icon, then just stays there forever. Workaround? None. Screenshot the greyed out screen so you can at least see, in a photo, whatever changes you made that are visible at the time, and redo it later on a real computer. 3.) numerous functions/formulas are missing. In the year 2026, with the chips in these iPads (especially the pro), there’s no reason whatsoever not to have a full version of excel here. If you can run it on a 15 year old desktop PC, you should be able to run it on a 2026 iPad Pro. Just saying. Overall rating -100 stars, for the 100+ lost minutes of work this app has lost me, this year alone. I actively hate it.

If I make a change on my iPhone and then try to exit out of the file Microsoft Excel just hangs and I have to force close Microsoft Excel. That results in me having server conflicts when I go and edit the desktop file. Also, even after deleting Microsoft Excel from my iPhone, the version, the latest version that was accessed by my iPhone is stuck in limbo and I cannot delete it or edit it.

reviews.title: Can’t change Margins on iPad?! …Still? In 2026?!
reviews.text:
Excel has been on the Ipad for well over a decade. I get it’s not meant as a full hearty laptop, but I still feel they should be doing their best to improve the costumer experience and usefulness of Excel and Word over fixing nuances like icons on the menu bar. 

I have the 12.9 Pro because it’s my main computer, easier for me to carry, and with an external keyboard, it’s more expensive than a laptop. Limiting margins is one of the greatest frustrations because excel is column and row based application so the print limit of 1” on all four sides is ridiculous and incredibly frustrating.

There’s also freezing and curser issues iPad. I’ll make an error and often can’t place my curser in the exact spot to fix it so I have to retype that cell / formula. This curser issue happens in Word sometimes too. 

The iPad is very popular, so I wish more effort could be given to smoothing out the business operations a little because it’s too much to have to try to go back and forth between devices. I switched to the iPad because I no longer deal in more complex spreadsheets, but I still want the basics…like a bigger printable workspace.

Sorry, I am just feeling frustrated by this today.

The app really limits usability. Especially the file viewing setup. There is no way to customize the recents page, of size of each thumbnail. They take up the entire display and also do not display the actual sheet, its just blank. 
Recent files are not shared across devices, so when I create a file on my ipad, it wont show up anywhere on my recents on my phone unless I manually search for it. Theres no way to sort files when browsing. I frequently get in app errors. Like failed to remove from list, or failed to close, things like that. reviews.text:

It doesn’t do basic things well anymore: you can’t reliably move between sheets (you have to leave the document or close the app to make the option reappear). You can’t access the ribbon menu after selecting something (you have to force close the app!). Despite this, I managed to create a hefty spreadsheet over a few weeks for a personal project. I no longer can access it because the app keeps freezing on the initial screen or when I open up the spreadsheet it’ll load a small portion of it then the rest remains white and freezes. The iCloud icon is stuck on endless loading. I’ve tried updating my iOS, reinstalling the app, clearing data etc. nothing is working. I just renewed my 365 subscription for this and I’m pretty annoyed that the thing I’m paying for isn’t working. This app definitely needs a lot of fixing so be warned. 

*Update*

They have made it even worse after the update. I have now lost everything in multiple workbooks. Luckily, I made backups but the app straight up deleted everything inside multiple workbooks. The issue happens if you’re using a file saved on your phone. If your app crashes (which it does frequently) and you’re in the middle of making changes to it, the next time you open that workbook literally everything will be wiped clean. I’ve also had to delete and reinstall the app 3 to 4 times a day because the ability to copy paste into the formula bar disappears. You can’t even move to a new line when typing.
